properties.headline: Cold Weather Advisory issued November 18 at 10:20PM PST until November 20 at 8:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Cold conditions with temperatures between 33 and 36 degrees.

* WHERE...Interior Monterey County and the Santa Lucia Range, Most of
San Benito County and the Cholame Hills in Southeast Monterey
County, North Bay Interior Mountains, North Bay Interior Valleys,
and Eastern Santa Clara Hills.

* WHEN...For the first Cold Weather Advisory, from 1 AM to 8 AM PST
Friday. For the second Cold Weather Advisory, from 1 AM to 8 AM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
properties.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 4:56PM PST until November 20 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45
AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.
properties.instruction:
